50473138.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to BRPF1 (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli strains BL21 (DE3) cells by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Inc.) at 25 °C. The protein (TRIM24(PHD-bromo) or BRPF1) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.5, and concentrated to 100 μM. The ligand (8i) was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer to a final concentration of 100 μM. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the ligand was loaded into the syringe (200 μL). The experiment consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The binding affinity (Kd) was calculated from the integrated heat of binding. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the mean values are reported. The buffer was used as a control to subtract the heat of dilution.

50473137.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human His-tagged TRIM24-PHD/bromodomain expressed in Escherichia coli strains BL21 (DE3) cells by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Experimental Methods - ITC Measurements: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Inc.) at 25 °C. The protein (TRIM24-PHD/bromodomain) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.5, and concentrated to 100 μM. The ligand (8i) was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer to a final concentration of 100 μM. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the ligand was loaded into the syringe (200 μL). The experiment consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. A blank experiment was performed by titrating the ligand into buffer alone. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The binding affinity (Kd) was calculated from the integrated heat of binding.
